topIssues.title: feat(lifeops): deliver Bettina owner-private family operations MVP
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The Bettina pilot needs one owner-private family operations journey that is reproducible from GitHub and verifiable through the deployed product. The current VPS runs unpublished local commits and has no complete acceptance path for agreement knowledge, bounded guest access, linked Google calendar sync, school-calendar automation, coordination packets, or approved iMessage delivery.

## Scope

- Stabilize remote pairing with instance-bound, machine-readable failures and public-origin acceptance.
- Store immutable parenting-agreement artifacts with reviewed page-cited obligations.
- Keep owner-only access by default; make pins independent of bounded verified guest grants.
- Preserve the built-in Eliza Calendar and add durable two-way linked Google events with conflict, replay, quarantine, and disconnect semantics.
- Add the guarded monthly Concord school-calendar PDF discovery/hash/diff workflow with owner-selected automatic application of validated changes.
- Add a versioned monthly coordination packet and neutral approval-gated external draft; exclude expenses.
- Add deterministic daily calendar cards and secure approved iMessage/Blooio delivery.
- Consolidate the pilot onto the reviewed Eliza runtime and deploy an immutable merged SHA to Bettina VPS.

## Acceptance

- Every PDD requirement has an automated or explicit live gate in a traceability matrix.
- Relevant package tests, PGlite restart/concurrency/adversarial tests, app E2E, five visual-audit cycles, root verify/test, and canonical evidence review pass at the exact PR SHA.
- Fresh-browser public pairing works and negative/replay cases fail distinctly.
- Agreement review, page citations, pins, grants, expiry, revocation, export, and deletion dependencies work through UI and APIs.
- Eliza Calendar works without Google; `shawgotbags@gmail.com` proves bidirectional create/update/delete/conflict/idempotency on a test calendar.
- The current Concord district page resolves the PDF; the owner-selected automatic mode applies validated imports and revisions, identical reruns are recorded no-ops, and changed revisions only update workflow-owned events. Ambiguous or invalid source data remains quarantined for review; review mode still requires an exact-plan approval.
- Approved iMessage/Blooio delivery is proven on the real configured edge with unauthorized sender, signature, replay, and tamper rejection.
- The deployed process reports the merged SHA, passes restart persistence, and has no auth, credential, embedding, migration, duplicate-send, or unclassified runtime errors.

## Related work

- #17176 calendar source completeness
- #17179 co-parent scenario corpus
- #17181 school calendar ingestion
- #23103 document entitlements and pins
- #22787 iMessage/Blooio readiness

## Evidence policy

Mocked or authored-scenario success is intermediate evidence only. Provider-backed Google and iMessage acceptance, exact deployed provenance, database rows, logs, screenshots/video, and reviewed evidence bundles are required before closure.

## Clarified school-calendar requirement

The owner explicitly selected “Auto-apply school calendar changes” when asked to choose the update policy. This supersedes the older PDD SCH-13 wording that required approval of every revision. The runtime already exposes explicit review/automatic modes (merged in #30957); preserve that choice. Update the PDD and traceability matrix to match this decision. Automatic mode is not permission to modify unrelated events or silently accept ambiguous source data.

topIssues.title: feat(lifeops): selected correspondence intake and missing-information review for monthly packets
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Observed product gap

The owner-facing monthly packet can generate a draft from calendar, school, approved obligations, household coordination and owner travel records. `FamilyWorkflowRuntimeService.collectCanonicalClaims` does not ingest selected emails or messages. The Family Operations packet surface has no selected-correspondence intake or persisted missing-information review. A successful draft self-send therefore does not complete the requested monthly coordination workflow.

## Required behavior

- Import or paste selected correspondence, preserving complete source content, source identity, date, provenance and private audience. Do not require account-wide history access for the first useful packet. Use canonical document/media storage and connector identity; do not add a second file store.
- Extract proposed facts and requests with source citations, then let the owner correct and confirm them. Keep unknown, conflicting and absent information distinct. Unavailable inference must be visible and must not fabricate a completed extraction.
- Ask about missing parenting schedule, school, agreement obligations, travel/consent/health and unanswered requests. Persist answers and an explicit no-updates answer; empty or failed input is not no updates. Expenses remain excluded.
- Bind reviewed facts and owner answers to their target month and source revision. Regeneration, reload and restart preserve accepted input without duplicating it or silently restoring withdrawn information.
- Carry unanswered requests forward under the existing bounded carry-forward policy; resolved requests must stop recurring. The owner can inspect the source and prior state.
- Revalidate source access and recipient sharing before external draft creation and dispatch. Raw private correspondence, unreviewed claims and owner-only notes cannot become an external email merely because they were selected for intake.
- Reuse immutable packet/draft versions, stale-approval rejection, canonical approval queue, exact sender/recipient bindings and existing sent-record export. Intake never sends an email or message.

## Acceptance

Use complete synthetic email/message sources, a private note, a conflicting source pair and a prior unanswered request. Exercise the real UI → authenticated API → canonical storage → model extraction → owner review → packet → exact approved self-email flow. Verify source hashes/citations and the sent export independently. Repeat refresh/restart, stale edits, withdrawn source, revoked recipient, denied principal, model outage and duplicate import cases; no repeated send is permitted. Capture current-head desktop/mobile rest/hover states, MP4, backend/frontend logs and applicable live-model/provider receipts.

Existing transport and synthetic browser evidence in PR #31032 remains useful but does not satisfy this acceptance. This is a concrete missing consumer workflow, not a coverage-only task.

topIssues.title: Improve context + clean up context slop
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Optimize the context sent to the model so action/tool search works efficiently and the agent gets only what it needs to complete the task.

## Detailed Description

**Estimate:** 5 working days. **After:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/31014

Use the existing context editor and trajectory viewer.

- Review representative runs to identify unnecessary instructions, duplicate context, irrelevant provider output and oversized tool descriptions/results.
- Improve context selection and composition: include what the current task needs and retrieve additional context when needed. Remove redundancy at its source rather than silently cutting off payloads.
- Verify action/tool search finds the right capabilities with concise queries, useful rankings and minimal repeated searches. Fix missed tools, irrelevant matches and unnecessary tool loading.
- Use the existing edit, rerun and compare loop to measure input tokens, retrieval overhead, latency, tool choices and task success. Record the context changes and model/settings used.
- Check both simple and multi-step tasks. Reduce context without losing required facts, tool arguments or reliable task completion.

- Correct Cloud usage attribution before comparing runs: map native `promptTokens`/`completionTokens` to the usage-event `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` contract in buffered, SSE and non-SSE fallback paths. Check current behavior and reuse applicable #27744 work.
- Verify emitted input/output/total counts match gateway usage, including a final SSE usage-only frame. Verify downstream cost estimates use the real counts when gateway cost is absent; retain unknown usage as unavailable. This fixes telemetry, not server-side credit debits.

Cloud token counts #27732 is consolidated here within the same five-day allocation. Original reproduction and consumer details remain linked in that issue.

**Done when:** before/after trajectories show lower unnecessary context and efficient action/tool search, with the agreed tasks still completing correctly. Record token and latency changes, failures and any tradeoffs. Missing usage stays unknown; estimates are labeled.

Reruns, comparison, validation and targeted fixes are included in the five days. This ticket does not build another context editor.

topIssues.title: fix(app): expose actionable local backup size-limit failures
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
The running macOS app cannot create a backup of the current agent state, and the dialog hides the deterministic size rejection behind “Backup failed.” Retrying the same state cannot succeed.

Reproduced in signed development bundle a0de6f6cc43e8c086f12a2fbf1b932b91a7bee63: Settings → Backups → Back up agent → Create Backup. The dialog remains open with an error; no backup was created and no restore was attempted. Sanitized runtime diagnostic at 2026-09-06T19:11:54.645Z: `Snapshot refused during file capture: source budget exceeded`.

`POST /api/backups` calls `createLocalAgentBackup`, which uses the v1 snapshot path. `AgentSnapshotBudgetExceededError` already carries code, stage, observed bytes and limit bytes. The route catches every failure and sends generic HTTP 500. The v1 shared restore ceiling is 128 MiB; source capture also accounts for allocation overhead. Do not raise that cap, truncate content, or omit state to make this test pass.

Acceptance:

- Translate the known typed budget rejection to a structured, safe response without filesystem paths or database diagnostics.
- Show an actionable size-limit explanation in the native backup dialog and distinguish it from a retryable transport/storage failure.
- Exercise the real route/error boundary and UI consumer, including an ordinary unexpected failure; preserve full backup data and existing limits.
- Confirm whether the supported large-state local backup path is the existing v2 streaming implementation. Keep full backup success explicitly unverified until a created artifact is inspected and a restore is verified in isolated state.
- Capture the native result in the rebuilt revision; the current observation is a failure, not acceptance proof.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): reconcile subscription lifecycle and primary billing policy
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Advances #23093, #23094 and #23095; also supplies the consent-bound registration prerequisite for #30638. These issues remain open. Pending hosted and live-integration acceptance.

# Behavior

Stripe terminal observations now publish lifecycle history, receipt, entitlement projection, policy generation and cancellation notice intent atomically. A failed write rolls back the whole transition. Historical event replay cannot restore older subscription authority.

Session-authorized managers can schedule and undo period-end cancellation. Commands record dispatch provenance before mutation and verify canonical Customer/subscription state before publication. Uncertain outcomes reconcile by retrieval without an automatic second mutation. Undo requires the captured schedule lineage to remain valid before dispatch. Tenant-scoped pending-command pagination exposes stale source identity and command uncertainty. Scheduling cancellation preserves current access until an effective terminal transition.

Existing-v1 paid renewal verifies the complete invoice, subscription, Customer, PaymentIntent, captured charge and catalog binding before granting allowance. Only a full captured, non-refunded, unadjusted monthly payment for an adjacent effective period can publish. Duplicate invoice/event delivery cannot grant twice. Unsupported observations retain retryable incident state.

Resource and inference admission use the same primary policy generation as billing snapshots. Cached paid state refreshes after a committed Free transition; missing or ambiguous required canonical authority is unavailable. Canonical-none non-subscriber accounts retain their existing legacy fallback. New allowance reservations and snapshot spendability share current organization/source/projection/period/grant identity checks. Denied spending is explicitly unavailable while ledger amounts remain intact; eligible exhausted allowance reports an observed zero. Historical reservations retain their settlement/refund ownership.

Generic app billing registration records owner and infrastructure-payer provenance and creates individual buyer accounts only after existing app consent. Merchant and subscription policy remain explicitly unconfigured. Cancellation notices have immutable identity, one durable attempt and distinct accepted/rejected/uncertain/unavailable outcomes. Dispatch requires server-approved per-revision recipients, content and delivery window. Missing policy does not send; uncertain SMTP acceptance does not trigger automatic resend or prove delivery.

The existing authenticated Stripe cron also recovers missed terminal observations using read-only canonical SDK requests. Durable leases, retry scheduling and complete-body deadlines bound provider work without retrying writes. Recovery publishes source/projection/generation/notice atomically and preserves webhook watermark provenance. Matching later events use a no-op only for a durably applied recovery revision with a coherent projection; ordinary webhook behavior is unchanged. Independent cron lanes retain failures and successful receipts separately.

# Validation and review

Current head `2d85438b7c8cd54a38227dd3376e10033a07e5d6`, rebased on `c2d55bf5e460055c19fb0c8bdfe217e4f1b2c8d8` (41 commits).

- Normal pinned install passed (Bun1.3.14 / Node24.15.0); private dependency paths verified after repairing three old local dependency links. Source unchanged.
- Current root verification:377/377 tasks, zero cache hits, all audits passed; single-worker Turbo9m21s, unchanged checkout.
- Current login/subscription checks:90 tests257 assertions passed, including manager authorization, commands and nonce exchange.
- Four current-head actual database captures passed and were inspected; complete records below.
- Prior full shared775e:12,801 passed243 skipped0failed81,637 assertions. Prior fullAPI775e:603 isolated files,6,514 passed4skipped0failed37,154 assertions. Prior post-inference-rebase suites127/502 passed. These remain historical receipts, not full-suite claims for this head.

Hosted failures from the initial revision were diagnosed and independently reviewed: seven fixed Stripe fixture sentinels now have an exact-path AND exact-line scanner exception (41-commit scan passes; changed literal and unlisted-path controls still fail); the PostgreSQL observer refreshes activity snapshots inside its transaction; two payment-replay assertions preserve every queue counter while accepting added cron lane receipts.
